title: DeliChess: A Multi-party Dialogue Dataset for Deliberation in Chess Puzzle Solving
abstract: arXiv:2606.04987v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Multi-party dialogue is a critical setting for studying collaborative reasoning and decision-making, yet existing datasets rarely focus on structured, reasoning-intensive tasks. We introduce DeliChess, a dataset of group deliberation dialogues in which participants collaboratively solve multiple-choice chess puzzles. Participants first answer independently, then engage in multi-party deliberation and revise their individual answers. The dataset comprises 107 sessions containing 321 puzzle discussions across 24 unique positions, with full transcripts, pre- and post-deliberation choices, and utterance-level annotations of communicative function, epistemic stance, and usefulness in supporting deliberation. Our analyses show that greater diversity in initial solution quality is associated with larger gains, while answer trajectories reveal how deliberation can recover, discover, or lose strong answers. translated_title: DeliChess：一个用于国际象棋谜题求解审议的多方对话数据集
translated_abstract: 多方对话是研究协作推理与决策的关键场景，然而现有数据集很少关注结构化、推理密集型的任务。我们提出了DeliChess，这是一个群体审议对话数据集，参与者在其中协作解决多选式的国际象棋谜题。参与者首先独立作答，随后进行多方审议并修改各自答案。该数据集包含107个会话，涵盖24个独特棋局上的321次谜题讨论，并配有完整的对话转录文本、审议前后的答案选择，以及话语层面的交流功能、认知立场和支持审议有用性的标注。我们的分析表明，初始答案质量的多样性越高，审议带来的收益越大；同时，答案轨迹揭示了审议如何能够恢复、发现或丢失优质答案。
tldr: 该论文构建了首个多方审议对话数据集DeliChess，让参与者协作解决国际象棋谜题，揭示出初始答案多样性越高审议收益越大，以及审议过程中群体答案可被恢复、发现或丢失的规律。
